acceptance_row: Settings UI -> authenticated public API -> LocalControl -> same RuntimeClient -> asynchronous RuntimeHost management -> native config save/readback. This report assesses SOURCE safety, not installed/UI/PG acceptance.

findings.title: Management can initiate its config PUT after its authority deadline
findings.exact_input_or_timing: Valid save command for openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol/xhigh with a current generation=0, epoch=1 grant. Management startup/health completion crosses the absolute deadline before the next watchdog turn. _settings_native then invokes configure and PUT without checking state/deadline. _settings_run checks authority only after configure returns.
findings.expected: A config mutation not yet sent must be refused when authority has expired. Retiring the operation as INDETERMINATE after the mutation is not a pre-effect fence.
findings.actual: Real source Host/RuntimeClient UDS and an owned inert child reach the mocked native PUT endpoint after monotonic_ns >= deadline_ns. That endpoint physically writes an owned marker file once. The operation is then INDETERMINATE. The identical [False] control writes before the deadline and is CONFIRMED. Both children are reaped.
findings.proof_boundary: Native HTTP/config are doubles. The negative deliberately holds the synthetic health completion synchronously until the real grant expires, exposing the scheduling window before the watchdog executes; it does not mutate the clock, deadline, watchdog or product code. This demonstrates missing dispatch fencing, not an installed native filesystem write or a measured PG Stop overlap.
findings.minimum_remedy: Revalidate management state/current generation/epoch/deadline immediately before each new effectful dispatch after awaits. Carry revocable authority through the native save/commit boundary if the contract prohibits local writes after revocation; an asynchronous watchdog and a post-result check alone cannot establish that stronger guarantee. Add the same positive/expired control and a pending-save Stop/expiry commit-cut regression without extending grants/deadlines.

findings.title: Foreign config is accepted and preserved once the three selected values match
findings.native_static_anchor: hermes_cli/config.py at pinned ee5ee84:2422-2461; merge_existing deep-merges omitted raw sections at 2445-2447
findings.exact_input_or_timing: Existing config contains the exact model/provider, reasoning_effort=xhigh, reasoning_overrides={'gpt-6.1-sol':'xhigh'}, auth.adopt_external_logins=false, plus fallback_model={'provider':'openrouter','model':'foreign-model'}, auxiliary.vision with a foreign provider/model/base_url, and extra keys in agent/auth. All values are synthetic.
findings.expected: Refuse unsupported/foreign configuration before mutation; do not present a narrow approved readback while retaining unapproved fallback, auxiliary or auth/config sections.
findings.actual: saved_selection accepts the foreign config, GET returns the exact selected triple, PUT returns {'ok':true}, and a disk-backed native-writer double with the pinned merge_existing semantics preserves every foreign field. The public projection hides the unsupported data. A minimal exact allowed configuration is accepted on the same projection.
findings.proof_boundary: Executed adapter projection/config_operation; the native module import is replaced by a declared disk-backed double. Native broad merge behavior was independently read statically, not executed. No actual personal configuration or credentials were accessed; no claim of observed provider fallback execution.
findings.minimum_remedy: Validate the complete allowed raw configuration shape and exact scalar types before save and after readback, including all top-level and nested fields and any narrowly enumerated canonical fields actually added by the pinned writer. Reject unknown/fallback/aux/auth sections rather than silently preserving or stripping them. Keep the native store as the owner; do not add a second config store or weaken merge safety for unrelated native callers.

findings.title: Stop before the scheduled worker starts leaves a permanently PENDING receipt
findings.exact_input_or_timing: Admit a valid read command via _settings_start, then execute stop before the newly created settings_task gets its first event-loop turn.
findings.expected: Stop/drain must publish a terminal not-executed/unavailable/indeterminate operation receipt even when cancellation occurs before the worker's try/except has run.
findings.actual: settings_task is done and cancelled; Host state is STOPPED and drained=true, but settings_result remains PENDING. settings_status returns that retained PENDING forever. UI keeps the pending state and disables a fresh read/save; exact-operation recovery cannot change this terminal task's receipt.
findings.proof_boundary: Deterministic direct SOURCE owner scheduling cut. No subprocess is started and no native operation occurs. Actual UDS arrival scheduling for this exact prestart ordering was not separately exercised.
findings.minimum_remedy: Finalize every admitted operation in the owner's stop/finalization path (or a completion callback), including tasks cancelled before entry. Do not rely only on the coroutine's cancellation handler. Preserve no-resend semantics and test prestart and already-running cancellation separately.

findings.title: Native save ACK accepts numeric 1 as boolean true
findings.exact_input_or_timing: Native PUT reply is JSON {'ok':1}; subsequent GET returns the exact requested selection.
findings.actual: Python dict equality treats 1 as True; configure accepts the malformed ACK and returns success after readback.
findings.proof_boundary: SOURCE decoder with mocked native endpoint. Exact GET readback remains required, so this does not independently prove a false configuration value or inference readiness.
findings.minimum_remedy: Require exact dict field set {'ok'} and result['ok'] is True. Add 1/1.0/unknown-field negatives while preserving the canonical positive.

positive_observations: Provider mutations use authenticated public routes and existing LocalControl, then the supervisor's same RuntimeClient. Tested public session/CSRF denials and unchanged 4096/4097 public/control byte limits passed with explicit auth/DB doubles.

Host state separates MANAGEMENT from READY; actual management producer has null bootstrap_inventory and never sets assessment_ready/inference_ready. Save does not claim authentication or model compatibility.

Management-vs-execution state checks and single active settings task exist; author busy/execution-denial/Stop/expiry/expired-idle and cancelled-exchange cases passed. These do not prove PG overlapping transactions or the missing sink fence.
Management launch supplies an explicit isolated environment rather than copying ambient variables. Owned inert-child environment and stop/reap test passed; no personal data was used.

Lost replies do not automatically resend mutations; exact-operation receive-only status is separate from new settings authority. Bounded retained operation receipts are distinct from new native execution.

Existing 3600 command, 4096 local-control and 65536 runtime frame limits were not increased; existing authority deadlines/grants were not extended. The reviewer expiry fixture uses a shorter grant only.
limits_and_deferred: SOURCE only. No installed native import/boot, OCI, database, OAuth, provider, target or external network effects. Native filesystem save/readback/restart remains NOT_RUN.

No real browser QA; component test and static async-auth inspection do not certify click/keyboard/reload/layout behavior. Prestart pending receipt creates a concrete source-level UI recovery consequence, not a claimed browser reproduction.
No real PostgreSQL overlap/Stop/lease transaction proof. Source authority/auth doubles must not be credited as that proof.
No namespace/PID1 drain certification. Real owned source children were joined; outside PID1, product UNCERTAIN is preserved rather than changed into STOPPED acceptance.
